sections.h2: Who records deeds in Tipton County?
sections.html:
The Tipton County Register of Deeds records them. Claudia Peeler is the Register, and the office takes mail at PO Box 626, Covington, TN 38019, with deed questions at 901-476-0204. The county's own page cites Tennessee Code 66-24-101 for the office's main duty, which is recording deeds and other instruments the law requires or allows to be filed.

The same page lists what can be recorded: deeds, powers of attorney, mortgages, marriage settlements, plats and military discharges. The Register also collects and accounts for the fees and taxes that go with each filing. For a home sale, that usually means the deed from the seller to the buyer and the buyer's deed of trust if a loan is involved. The title company or closing attorney normally takes the documents to the office.

Ask the office for its current hours and whether it accepts electronic filing, because the county's page does not describe either. Lookup of property records is separate: the Assessor's parcel search is at tiptontn.geopowered.com/PropertySearch.

sections.h2: What is Tipton County, and why do deeds here move through Covington?
sections.html:
Tipton County lies on the western end of Tennessee along the Mississippi River, with Covington as the county seat. The county was created on October 29, 1823 from part of Shelby County and covers 473 square miles. U.S. Highway 51 passes through Covington. Munford, Atoka, Brighton, Mason, Burlison, Garland and Gilt Edge are the other incorporated places.

The recorded history of land here is long. Randolph was the most important shipping point in Tennessee by 1830, rail reached Mason in December 1855 and Covington in July 1873, and the 1811 and 1812 New Madrid earthquakes moved the river and left communities such as Reverie on the Arkansas side. The county's western boundary still follows the old river channel. That is why parcels near the river can carry odd descriptions, and a seller with riverfront land should expect the title company to read the legal description with care.

Census Bureau QuickFacts for Tipton County:

  • 62,287 residents in July 2025, with 25,033 housing units
  • 76.3% owner-occupied housing for 2020 to 2024
  • Median owner-occupied value of $240,600, and median gross rent of $1,013
  • 139 building permits in 2025
  • 91.4% of residents in the same house a year earlier, a sign of settled ownership

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Tipton County?
sections.html:
The county lists its recording fees on the Register's page, using the standard Tennessee schedule. An ordinary instrument of one or two pages is $10.00, and each page after the second is $5.00. Add a $2.00 data processing fee per document and a $1.00 clerk's fee whenever state tax is paid.

ItemFeeSource
Instrument of one or two pages$10.00Tipton County Register of Deeds
Each additional page after two$5.00Tipton County Register of Deeds
Plat$15.00Tipton County Register of Deeds
Data processing, per document$2.00Tipton County Register of Deeds
Clerk's fee, only when state tax is paid$1.00Tipton County Register of Deeds
Certified copy, per page$1.00Tipton County Register of Deeds
Military dischargeNo chargeTipton County Register of Deeds

For a four-page warranty deed on which state tax is paid, the recording charge is $10 for the first two pages, $10 for the next two, $2 for data processing and $1 for the clerk's fee, a total of $23. A release or assignment added to an instrument costs $5.00 for each one after the first. UCC fixture filings are $13.00, and UCC filings over 10 pages add $0.50 per page.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax and mortgage tax apply in Tipton County?
sections.html:
Two state taxes are collected at the Register's counter. The realty transfer tax is $0.37 for every $100 of the purchase price, and the mortgage tax is $0.115 for every $100 of debt, with the first $2,000 of the debt exempt. The Tennessee Department of Revenue posts the same rates, and the county's page shows them as the state conveyance tax and the state mortgage tax.

The numbers add up fast on a typical sale. A home sold at the Census median of $240,600 produces a transfer tax of about $890. A $200,000 loan produces a mortgage tax of $227.70, since the taxable amount is $198,000. Both are separate from the recording fees in the table above.

Who pays which tax is set in the purchase contract and shown on the settlement statement, so confirm it with the closing agent before signing. County property tax is a separate matter handled by the Trustee, and the Register does not collect it.

sections.h2: How does recording a deed connect to the Tipton County tax bill?
sections.html:
Timing matters. The Trustee mails each tax notice in the first week of October to the person who owned the property on January 1. If the new deed is recorded before the September deadline, a duplicate notice also goes to the new owner. A buyer whose deed is recorded later may not receive a bill at all and should call the Trustee at 901-476-0211.

The 2026 county rate is $1.3417 per $100 of assessed value, and residential property is assessed at 25 percent. Taxes can be paid without interest through February 28, and 1.5 percent interest is added each month starting March 1. Before a deed goes to the Register, steps worth completing are:

  • Ask the Trustee for the status of the current tax year on the parcel
  • Check whether a city bill, such as Covington's, is also open
  • Confirm the legal description and parcel number match the deed
  • Bring checks for the recording fee and the state tax if the title company has not

sections.h2: What is the property fraud alert, and who should sign up?
sections.html:
The Register offers a free Property Fraud Alert through its computer vendor. Once an owner enrolls, an email arrives whenever a document is recorded under a name the owner has added. A seller who just closed, or an heir managing a family house, can use it to watch for filings under the old owner's name. The enrollment steps on the county's page are:

  • Have a valid email address ready
  • Go to www.mylandalert.com and click Register in the upper left
  • Accept the terms at the bottom of the page and enter the email address
  • Click the verification link, choose a password, and add the names to watch

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Tipton County, TN?
faqs.a: Record it with the Tipton County Register of Deeds in Covington. The office mails to PO Box 626, Covington, TN 38019, and answers deed questions at 901-476-0204.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Tipton County?
faqs.a: A deed of one or two pages costs $10.00, plus $5.00 for each extra page, a $2.00 data processing fee and a $1.00 clerk's fee when state tax is paid.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a Tipton County home sale?
faqs.a: The state realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of the purchase price. On a $240,600 sale that is about $890.

faqs.q: Is there a mortgage tax in Tipton County?
faqs.a: Yes. The state mortgage tax is $0.115 per $100 of debt after the first $2,000, so a $200,000 loan carries $227.70.

faqs.q: Can I get alerts if someone records a document against my property?
faqs.a: Yes. The Register offers a free Property Fraud Alert at mylandalert.com that emails you when a document is recorded under a name you enroll.
